script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SUBURBAN NEIGHBORHOOD - DAY

A beautiful sunny day. Children are playing in the yard. Families are walking their dogs. A white picket fence separates the idyllic scene from the world beyond.

INT. JENKINS LIVING ROOM - DAY

MARY JENKINS (40s) sits on the couch, laptop open in front of her. Her husband PETER (50s) enters the room.

PETER
(cheerfully)
How's the writing going?

MARY
(sighs)
Slowly. I just can't seem to find the right balance between my creativity and reality.

PETER
(placing a hand on her shoulder)
You'll figure it out. You always do.

MARY
(looking up at him)
I hope so. I want this to be my breakthrough.

PETER
(smiling)
We all have big dreams.

INT. JENKINS KITCHEN - NIGHT

Mary is chopping vegetables for dinner while her daughter, EMMA (13) does her homework at the table.

EMMA
(looking up from her book)
Mom, can I bring a friend over for dinner on Friday?

MARY
(pausing to look at her)
Of course, honey. Who is it?

EMMA
(grinning)
Josh. He's really good at science. Maybe he can help me with some of my projects.

MARY
(smiling)
That's wonderful, Emma. I'm glad you're making new friends.

INT. JENKINS DEN - DAY

Mary sits at her desk, surrounded by stacks of books and papers. Her phone rings. She answers it.

MARY
(on phone)
Hello? Yes, this is Mary Jenkins.

(pauses)

MARY
(excitedly)
Really? You'd consider me for a writing fellowship? That's amazing!

(pauses)

MARY
(gratefully)
Thank you so much. I'll prepare everything you need and send it right over.

INT. JENKINS LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Peter sits in an armchair, reading a newspaper. Mary enters the room, her face glowing with excitement.

MARY
(excitedly)
I got it, Peter! The writing fellowship!

PETER
(stands up and hugs her)
I'm so proud of you, Mary!

MARY
(tearfully)
Thank you. I couldn't have done it without your support.

INT. SCHOOL LIBRARY - DAY

Emma sits at a table, surrounded by her classmates. They're working on a group project. Josh, her friend, sits next to her.

EMMA
(frustrated)
I don't get it. How are we going to make a model volcano that actually erupts?

JOSH
(smiling)
Leave that to me. I've got a few tricks up my sleeve.

INT. JENKINS DEN - NIGHT

Mary types away at her laptop, the deadline for her fellowship application fast approaching.

Suddenly, she receives an email. She opens it, her eyes wide.

MARY
(excitedly)
Peter! I got it! I've been accepted into the writing fellowship!

PETER
(jumps up and hugs her)
That's amazing, Mary! I'm so proud of you!

INT. SCHOOL AUDITORIUM - DAY

Emma and her classmates present their volcano project to the class. They all receive applause and praise for their hard work.

EMMA
(to Mary, during the car ride home)
I'm so proud of you, Mom. You're going to be a famous writer now!

MARY
(smiling)
Maybe one day, Emma. But for now, let's celebrate your hard work and your new friend.

INT. JENKINS DEN - NIGHT

Mary sits at her desk, her laptop open in front of her. She begins to type, her mind filled with ideas and possibilities.

PETER
(entering the room)
You look focused, Mary. What are you working on?

MARY
(looking up at him)
Just some ideas for my fellowship project. But it feels different this time. I know I can do it.

PETER
(sitting down next to her)
You always have. And I'll be here to support you every step of the way.

FADE OUT.

THE END
